question.prompt:
The five pieces shown below can be arranged to form four of the five figures below. Which figure cannot be formed?

[Figure 1](figures/2009_AMC_8_Q04_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The pieces are straight strips containing \(1,2,3,4,\) and \(5\) squares. Start with the longest strip: it needs five consecutive squares in one row or one column. In B, every horizontal or vertical run contains at most four squares. Turning the strip does not shorten it, so B cannot be formed.

We can check the other four figures by giving arrangements. Keep each figure in the orientation shown.

A: Put the five-square strip in the leftmost column and the four-square strip in the top four squares of the rightmost column. Put the three-square strip across the remaining bottom-row squares, the two-square strip across the two remaining squares just above them, and the single square in the last gap.

C: Fill the five rows with strips of lengths \(5,4,3,2,1\), from top to bottom.

D: Fill one column with the five-square strip. Split a second column into strips of lengths \(4\) and \(1\), and split the third into strips of lengths \(3\) and \(2\).

E: Fill the top row with the five-square strip. Put the four-square strip vertically in the four central squares below it. Fill the three squares immediately to its left with the three-square strip, and the three squares to its right with the two-square strip and the single square.

Each arrangement uses every piece once and covers its figure without gaps or overlaps. Thus the figure that cannot be formed is \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Find room for the longest strip
